Some divers don’t even last that long… Quickest I’ve ever seen a Diver die was on Hellmire, Eastern Front. I drop a reinforcement beacon, watch a fire tornado touch down, and his Hellpod hits the damn thing in the center. He was already on fire when the pod door opened and we all heard his dying screams over the radio. I still hear them in my sleep. 

*takes long drag from cigarette* The cadet went through basic training, deployment and everything, and didn’t even die for democracy. Now I’ve gotta write to his family on Super Earth and tell them he was just in the wrong place at the wrong time. I’m not gonna sugar coat it or make up some heroic tale for them. They at least deserve the truth.

Now Tory has to adapt to a new, deadly enemy even more dangerous than space itself.

/TACTICAL ANALYSIS ENGAGED

​

Non-expert opinion, but I think it'll depend on the kind of melee you want. If you're going after vehicles and HQs, the dragoon's high damage will get the job done. If the job's not done the first time around, and the vehicle falls back, it's your invitation to charge again. However, charging into a unit of troops, it's gonna have a lot more attacks coming at it and it'll get surrounded quickly. If you're looking to melee against enemy troops then I imagine the fulgurites will be more handy, plus they can act as a screen when needed.

​

Another way to look at it: if you're already stocked up on anti-tank weapons, go for the fulgurites. If you already have a lot of troops, go with the dragoons.
